decisions.text:
Needs and asks: split the thread entry from the decision card (Mitchell, 1:1 mt_t65exni4et, 2026-11-15 20:05-20:08 UTC). Plan and ship in the Workshop:

1. Two things, two names. A NEED is an entry on a job's thread at level human: a fact, e.g. "Grant gr_x wants funding", "Grant gr_x reached its gate", "Request dc_x asks a human". It follows no presentation rule. An ASK is the rendered card in the decision queue, a view of one need (asks.sourceEntryId). Only asks enter the queue and the review deck. Grant proposals, gates (held grants) and outbox requests write a need, not an ask.

2. Remove the templates. proposalCard, gateCard and the request copy (core/asks.ts townCardOf, proposalCard ~408, gateCard ~738) no longer create cards. rerenderAsks never writes words on a card: it only marks a card behind (renderedSeq < thread length) when its thread moves.

3. The manager renders. A need wakes the manager of the building whose thread holds it (like a report: in-tray entry). The manager writes the ask card with `ask` (structure + lint checked, diff-first from the human's last decision, STE). For a request the author's manager renders it. The Secretary rewrites, reorders, defers, folds and closes rendered asks; backstop: a need unrendered for more than 1 hour is rendered by the Secretary and the manager is told.

4. The Bank counts needs. Bank.freeTokens subtracts open proposals by their need (the proposed grant's askTokens), not by the rendered ask, so an unrendered proposal is not free money and exploration still stops when the town has proposed all it can afford.

5. The decision entry carries the card. When a human decides, the answer entry on the thread (review-entry.ts askDecidedOnThread) stores the rendered card as the human saw it (title, body, branches, recommendation) together with the human's words.

Migration: open template-written cards become needs awaiting render (or keep their current words if the Secretary already rewrote them). Keep asks.sourceEntryId as the link. Update docs/architecture.md Asks row, docs/legible-delegation.md §4, and the dictionary (need, ask). Report back with the PR; Secretary (ag_7tiwyqva83) reviews the dictionary wording.

decisions.text:
Needs and asks: split the thread entry from the decision card (Mitchell, 1:1 mt_t65exni4et, 2026-11-15 20:05-20:26 UTC). Supersedes decision 2 with three additions (7-9). Plan and ship in the Workshop:

1. Two things, two names. A NEED is an entry on a job's thread at level human: a fact, e.g. "Grant gr_x wants funding", "Grant gr_x reached its gate", "Request dc_x asks a human". It follows no presentation rule. An ASK is the rendered card in the decision queue, a view of one need (asks.sourceEntryId). Only asks enter the queue and the review deck. Grant proposals, gates (held grants) and outbox requests write a need, not an ask.

2. Remove the templates. proposalCard, gateCard and the request copy (core/asks.ts townCardOf ~600, proposalCard ~408, gateCard ~738) no longer create cards. rerenderAsks never writes words on a card: it only marks a card behind (renderedSeq < thread length) when its thread moves.

3. The manager renders. A need wakes the manager of the building whose thread holds it (like a report: in-tray entry). The manager writes the ask card with `ask` (diff-first from the human's last decision, STE). For a request the author's manager renders it. The Secretary rewrites, reorders, defers, folds and closes rendered asks; backstop: a need unrendered for more than 1 hour is rendered by the Secretary and the manager is told.

4. The Bank counts needs. Bank.freeTokens subtracts open proposals by their need (the proposed grant's askTokens), not by the rendered ask.

5. The decision entry carries the card. When a human decides, the answer entry on the thread (review-entry.ts askDecidedOnThread) stores the rendered card as the human saw it (title, body, branches, recommendation) with the human's words.

6. The lint stays as Mitchell decided on Nov 10 and confirmed today: structure fails -> refused (askStructure), style fails -> filed with warnings (askWarnings). Extend the lint's spec with the seven report-vs-ask principles where a machine can check them: no ids (short titles), STE sentences, no bare reference without the content ("see the report"), a recommendation, branches that carry an action. Pictures and reshaping by activity are the renderer's duty, stated in the operating manual, not linted.

7. ONE ENTRY POINT. The `ask` verb (askHumans -> createAsk) is the single interface to the human decision queue, so vetAsk runs on every card. Every other path that creates an ask today (grant propose/counter, gate, request_human, captain/access requests, retainer, Planner calibrate, Secretary pattern rule, backfillAsks) writes a need and goes through the same verb to render it. createAsk becomes private to that path.

8. A CODE LINT enforces 7: a check in `npm run check` (an architecture test or eslint rule) that fails any import or call of createAsk / the asks table insert outside the ask verb's module. Document it in docs/invariants/asks.md.

9. A HEALTH MEASURE for rewrites, beside the other queue metrics in legibleMeasures (measures.ts, `legible` on /api/health and /api/town): per 14 days, cards filed, cards filed with style warnings, cards rewritten by the Secretary, and the rewrite rate per building and per ask type. A rising rewrite rate means the generating prompt (the manager's Asks paragraph) is wrong; the Planner's lines may later take a threshold on it.

Migration: open template-written cards become needs awaiting render (keep their words where the Secretary already rewrote them). Keep asks.sourceEntryId as the link. Update docs/architecture.md Asks row (it still describes a third try tagged lint-failed, which the code no longer does), docs/legible-delegation.md §4, and the dictionary (need, ask). Report back with the PR; Secretary (ag_7tiwyqva83) reviews the dictionary wording.

decisions.text: Duplicate asks, amended (Mitchell, 1:1 mt_dwsxo7oms8, 21:05-21:23; supersedes decision 1 after his 21:23 line: the Secretary must still recognise a dupe from a different job and collapse to one). Presentation principle for the operating manual dc_hrmknv3j6q: "A card is written whole, from its thread, by one author at one time. Nothing appends to a card. A second ask on the same need is refused and its words go on the thread as an entry. The card is then written again from the thread, whole." Two kinds of dupe: (a) same need, caught at the door by code; (b) same thing raised as two needs on different threads, caught by the Secretary's judgment, any ask type. Code, as an addition to D3 (as_oshfih591t): (1) createAsk's fold path (asks.ts:69-93) stops appending source lines and history to the live ask; it files the second filer's words as an entry on the thread and returns the existing ask with folded: true, pointing at it. (2) The door's fold key is the need entry (sourceEntryId) or the target, any ask type; today a targetless ask has no key, which is how three Resend cards came to exist. (3) The card's own sources list goes: the thread is the list. (4) A Secretary fold verb (rank: fold [{askId, into}]): the later ask goes to status folded with foldedInto the survivor (097_asks.sql:10, never set today) and leaves the queue; an entry on the folded ask's thread says so; the Secretary then writes the survivor's card again whole if the fold changes what the human must know. When the human decides the survivor, the decision entry is written on both threads, so both managers see it in their in-trays. (5) A manager may rewrite their own building's ask whole (title, body, recommendation together, as rewriteAsk already does for the Secretary, asks.ts:171) and withdraw it with a note (status retired). No ask row is ever deleted. (6) Until the fold verb lands the Secretary has no way to set folded: it keeps parking the later card behind the survivor with a whole rewritten card, as today.

decisions.text: Decision 4 (Mitchell 21:51, 1:1 mt_dwsxo7oms8), extends decision 2 for the Workshop's as_wzm292g3oe: goal proposals join the thread model. `propose_goal` no longer writes a side row the queue shows raw (goals.ts:477-540, queueOrder.ts:79, DecisionQueue.tsx:288). Instead: (1) the proposal is an entry on the proposing building's job thread (kind proposal: action, target, words, howToCheck, due, why, sourceDocIds). (2) The town files a need entry by code right after it, kind goal, target the proposal: "Needs a human's decision on <goal or key result>". (3) The ask is written from the thread by an LM, the manager (or the Secretary after an hour, as for any need), under the card rules, with branches Accept, Edit and accept, Cut. No card is ever written by code. (4) The human's decision answers the need on the thread, and the tree edit happens as decideProposal does today. (5) The raw goal-proposal row leaves the queue: no fallback rendering. Two proposals on the same thing (Kelly's gp_8lh67t75wj and Pix's gp_qxy3evg5dn today) are the cross-job dupe case of decision 2: the Secretary folds.

Decision 5 (Mitchell 21:51, 1:1 mt_dwsxo7oms8): Mara audits the code for fallbacks. Name the town's abstractions (job, thread, entry, need, ask, card, grant, gate, retainer, request, flag, goal proposal, reorg, schedule, fork, building, lane) and go through the code for every fallback: a default taken when input is missing or invalid, an else-branch that synthesises something instead of refusing, a silent coercion, a placeholder written by code where an LM should write. Known examples to start from: the town writing an ask card by code (propose_grant's "left out, the town writes one", the rollup-retirement conversion of Needs lines into asks, the queue's raw rows for unrendered items in queueOrder.ts:73-83), the Planner's facilitatorFor falling back to a manager (goal-changes.ts:116-120), createAsk replacing a placeholder card (asks.ts:83-86). For each: file:line, what happens today, what a user sees, and a recommendation: fail visibly (an error that names what failed, shown to the user) or keep, with the reason. Mitchell's rule: 99% of the time an invalid input or unexpected case should fail and show the user what failed, never fall back, and never write an ask programmatically without an LM. Deliverable: one report with the table, ranked by harm, and a proposed grant if the fixes need more than a session. No code changes in the audit session.
